reviews.review:
A love letter to Starship Troopers, dwarves, and horde shooters alike. Kick back with friends as you mine minerals, traverse through gorgeous cave systems, kick a few thousand barrels, and crack a billion or so bug skulls along the way.

Pros:
- Weapon customization is extremely varied, and min-maxing my favorite weapons towards the best fit for a given playstyle gives me the same giddiness now as it did 500 hours ago when I revved up the game for the first time
- Game feel is second-to-none; landing headshots, kiting and bouncing on top of enemies, utilizing dwarf-specific abilities and movements to traverse the world and kill bugs all feel responsive, tight, and rewarding

- A world that's *full* of personality
- Beers that do nothing besides rocket you across the launch bay, make you see ghosts, and freeze you
- A jukebox full of decent music to dance to
- A consistent sense of humor, from incidental dwarf lines (I seem to hear a new one every time I play) to legitimately fun(ny) achievements and weapon mods
- Starship trooper references

- Peerless sound design
- Every gunshot and explosion has a weight and heft to it, from the ping of the M1 Garand's mag on reload to a grenade melting a bug's skull from across a giant cavern
- Enemy screams and grunts are descriptive and unique, helping players hear things before they can see them
- Peerless spatial sound that perfectly indicates direction and distance from everything; you really feel like you're in vast tunnels mining ♥♥♥♥ with three other short men

- Environments with absurd variety
- instanced biomes constantly being improved with new flora, fauna, and geographical anomalies that differentiate biomes from each other greatly ( steam vents, lava geysers, silicate harvesters slicing the ground, bioluminescent plants sparkling across the floor, nodules that explode when you shoot at them, slime pits, snow, sandstorms, useless crystals that jut from every wall and realistically reflect light)
- walls full of collectible plants, ores, chests, and bugs full of loot

- Extremely helpful and friendly community throughout my entire play time, and scaling difficulty based on players/ a robot helper on solo to let players who would prefer a single-player experience have an easier time of it

- Robust endgame

Cons:

- Game is still in beta, so there's definitely the occasional frustrating bug or two
- certain overclocks seem worthless or just downgrades from stock weapons
- some of the endgame content seems randomly harder than it should be (Cursite events can suck my nuts until they're smooth tbh)
- skilltree is getting a tweak (which it needs), but mostly railroads you into certain need-to-have perks at the time of this writing
- game RNG just ♥♥♥♥♥ you really hard sometimes out of nowhere (bugs spawn near-infinitely and not in a way where the designers might have intended)
- Game, even on highest difficulty, eventually becomes doable; let us suffer


The game is great, cover-to-cover, and it might legitimately be the best game I've played this decade. I couldn't recommend it highly enough. Rock and stone, brothers.
You should get this game for Karl.

It's like Minecraft but less building and more guns/monsters. 

Pros.
Lots of variety in different dwarf classes + character progression + customization
Each mission has it's own quirks and features to mix it up. Different environments, objectives, monsters
Lighting and art style looks great
Huge dopamine/adrenaline rush when encountering and surviving the monster hoards in higher difficulties
Comedic elements sprinkled in throughout game. especially in character voice lines
Constant new updates
One of those games where you can hop on with the bois for an hour and log off. 

Cons
Occasional fps drops. 
Need to convince other people to play to fully enjoy the game

One of the best co-op games out there. 10/10 Worth full price.
Fun, simple, and to the point. Recommend to anyone who enjoys coop play.
